AttemptID.description: The protocol attempt id signed into the callback token.
AttemptID.name: attemptID

actor_id.description: The registered actor this acknowledgement is recorded for. An acknowledgement nobody is attributable for is a record of nobody having understood anything, so it is required.

note.description: Free text from the acknowledging party. Documentary.

verdict.description: Optional, and only `proceed` is admitted. An actor that cannot proceed does not acknowledge; its dispatch is refused when the window closes and routes under `preflight_unacknowledged`.

Actor.description: One `actors` table row (task t15). Actor identity is append-only: a capability or endpoint change is a new row (a new `revision`), never an update to an existing one. `capabilities` and `metadata` are rendered verbatim — neither column ever holds a credential (`metadata.auth_token_env`, when set, names the environment variable a worker reads a token from, never the token value itself), so there is nothing to redact.

capabilities.description: Declared capabilities, as the row's own JSON value.

metadata.description: Open metadata, as the row's own JSON value.

ActorAvailability.description:
The capacity circuit breaker's state for this actor (task t9, migration 0020's `actor_availability` table). Absent entirely when the actor has never been paused — which is a different fact from a pause that has lapsed, and the two are deliberately distinguishable: a lapsed or cleared pause still renders, with `paused: false`.
Keyed by `actor_key`, so every revision of one identity reports the same availability: provider capacity belongs to the identity, not to one append-only registration revision. The pause is a DEADLINE, not a flag — `paused` is computed server-side against the database's own clock, so horizontally-scaled workers and API readers cannot disagree about it.

cleared_at.description: Present only when an operator ended the pause early (POST /v1alpha1/actors/{id}/resume), which is what keeps "it expired" and "a human let it back in" distinguishable afterwards.

detail.description: One human line naming what happened.

paused.description: Whether the pause is still in force right now. False means the deadline passed or an operator cleared it; the rest of this block is then the history of the pause that ended.

paused_until.description: When the actor becomes (or became) dispatchable again.

reason.description: The §13.5 error class that tripped the breaker — `capacity_exhausted` today.

retry_after_seconds.description: The provider's own Retry-After hint, in seconds. Absent when it named none — never `0`, which would read as "retry immediately". The worker caps how long a hint may actually pause an actor; this is the unclamped value the provider sent.

tripped_by_run_id.description: The dispatch that discovered the exhaustion, so "why is this paused" is answerable from the actor surface alone rather than by correlating timestamps against the event log.

category.description: The run category tag ("" is the explicit uncategorized bucket — never omitted, always present as a real value).

ActorCategoryBucket.description: One ActorStats.categories entry — an ActorStatsBucket plus the category tag it summarizes.

ActorDurationPercentiles.description: p50/p90/p99 (linear interpolation) over this actor's attempt durations (completed_at - started_at, in seconds), computed only over attempts that have actually completed.

ActorGradeAgg.description: One grades.proposed/grades.confirmed bucket: how many grade.schema.json records and their mean rating.

mean_rating.description: Absent — never a fabricated 0 — when count is 0: an average of zero opinions is undefined, not zero.

ActorGrades.description: Proposed (agent-origin opinion) and confirmed (a human's own direct opinion) grade aggregates evaluating this actor, kept as two separate numbers — never blended into one.

ActorLedgerAuthorityCount.description: How many ledger records this actor originated (`origin.actor_id`) at a given authority — every record_type, not only `claim`; PRD §10.4 uses "claim" generically for anything an agent asserts.

ActorNodeRunOutcome.description: One node-run participation bucket. `status` is `node_runs.status` (the engine's technical lifecycle state); `outcome` is `node_runs.outcome` (the PRD's domain outcome, e.g. "changes_required" — set only on a succeeded transition). The two are reported side by side, never conflated: a domain outcome is not a technical status. `outcome` is absent when the node run has none recorded yet (in progress, failed, cancelled, or contract-rejected).

ActorRetryBurn.description: "Attempts per completion": how many dispatch attempts this actor made in scope, against how many of the node runs it attempted actually reached `completed`.

attempts_per_completion.description: attempts / completed_node_runs. Absent — never a fabricated division — when completed_node_runs is 0.

ActorStats.description: GET /v1alpha1/actors/{id}/stats' payload (task t15). `total` is the all-categories aggregate, computed as its own query scope — never a client-side sum of `categories` (a percentile is not additive across subgroups).

ActorStatsBucket.description: One stats slice's numbers — either the all-categories `total` or one named `categories` entry (see ActorStats).

duration_percentiles.description: Absent when no attempt in this scope has completed yet.

usage.description: The §13.2 usage/cost rollup (task t2), scoped to this actor's own attempts.

actor_ref.description: The agent actor to dispatch to, as a component reference, e.g. `actor://company/codex-thor@sha256:...`.

instruction.description: What the actor is being asked to do. Rides as run input, never workflow content.

repo.description: The checkout path the actor works in. Rides as run input.

sandbox.description: Sandbox mode for the session (default `read-only`). Rides as run input.

success_outcome.description: The domain outcome name the task node declares (default `completed`); must match the workflow schema's outcomeName pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`.

timeout.description: The task node's attempt timeout as a Go-style duration literal (default `15m`). Workflow content: a different timeout renders to a different digest.

continuation_ref.description: Opaque handle offered by the actor for continuing this session.

preserve_branch.description: The branch name a bridge's preserve-on-failure plumbing commit (task t25, issue #49) actually created a ref for. Present only on an attempt whose bridge committed one -- most attempts, including every successful one, carry no such branch. A minted but never-committed name is never reported here.

preserve_pushed.description: Whether preserve_branch reached the bridge's configured remote (true) or exists only in the bridge host's local object database (false, the expected common case today -- bridge-host push credentials are unverified). Present only alongside preserve_branch.

preserve_remote.description: The remote name (e.g. "origin") the bridge attempted or reached the push against. Informational only -- never combined with preserve_branch to construct a forge URL; a client-side link may only come from configuration the operator actually set.

result.description: The attempt's reported output, as submitted. On a FAILED attempt it is the engine's diagnostic instead: {"error": {"class", "detail", "actor"?}}. `class` is the control plane's own PRD 13.5 classification and `detail` its one-line summary; `actor`, present only when the actor's error response carried something readable, is the ACTOR's own account of the refusal -- `message` (its error text), `class` (its class CLAIM, which is not adopted as the engine's), `body` (a snippet of a body that declared no error string), and `truncated`. Every string in the actor block is length-bounded and stripped of control characters at the dispatch seam: it is text an actor wrote, so treat it as data and never as markup.

supersedes.description: The id of the attempt record this one corrects, absent on every ordinary dispatch. Set by the late-callback reconciliation: a node run's deadline expires, the engine records a timed_out attempt, and the actor session it bounded later reports the tokens, model, termination reason and preserve branch of work that really happened. That report cannot commit workflow state (PRD 13.4) and does not rewrite the record it corrects (PRD 10.4) -- it is appended as a new attempt naming the old one. A node run therefore legitimately lists BOTH: read the superseding record as current and the one it names as history.

termination_reason.description: The provider-reported reason this attempt ended.

usage_model.description: Model attribution exactly as reported by the bridge. Explicit unknown sentinels are rendered verbatim and never collapsed to null.

decisions.description: Map of record id to verdict.

expected_ledger_version.description: The ledger version the caller expects to still hold. A mismatch is refused with 409, nothing written.

rationale.description: Why the reviewer decided this way — what they read, ran, or checked. Recorded on every review record the commit appends. A confirmation with no stated reason cannot be told apart from an unread one, so an empty rationale is refused with 400.

CreateGateReportRequest.description: One merge gate's whole finding. Every gate the workflow declared is listed, including the ones that measured nothing — a gate omitted because it did not apply is a gate the counts cannot report.

attempt_ref.description: Narrows the records to one attempt.

base_sha.description: What the candidate was compared against.

changed_files.description: The changed-file set every applicability decision below was made against. Recorded on the aggregate because "which files did you consider" is the first question anyone asks of a not-applicable count.

commit_sha.description: The candidate the gates ran against, full 40-character lowercase hex, read back from the worktree the suites actually ran in.

node_run_ref.description: Narrows the records to one node run.

package_commit_sha.description: When commit_sha is a post-merge candidate, the harvested package commit this combination contains. The control plane binds this to the run's measured handover while recording the verdict on the candidate itself.

ref.description: The handover ref that carried the commit, validated against the same `refs/culture-nodes/` fence a control-plane fetch is.

validator_actor_id.description: The registered actor identifying the deterministic producer. Must not be an actor registered as `human`.

attempt_ref.description: Narrows the grade to one attempt, when it is not about the whole node run.

category.description: Optional flat tag carried onto the grade record itself (documentary — see grade.schema.json). Per-actor stats (GET /v1alpha1/actors/{id}/stats) slice by the graded run's own category, not this field.

evaluated_actor_id.description: The actor being evaluated. Must not equal grading_actor_id — a grade where the two are equal is refused (no actor grades its own work).

grading_actor_id.description: The actor recording the grade. Its registered actor kind (human or agent) decides the record's origin, and therefore whether it lands confirmed (human) or proposed (agent).

node_run_ref.description: Narrows the grade to one node run, when it is not about the whole run.

rating.description: The evaluator's opinion score on a fixed 1-5 scale.

ledger_version.description: The run's ledger version this request was read at.

reviewer_actor_id.description: The human actor the review is bound to, and the origin stamped on every review record the commit appends. Must be registered with kind `human`.

category.description: Optional flat tag (task t3), e.g. `review`, `audit`, `explore`, `implement`, `docs` — a cheap-to-change label, not a fixed taxonomy, so per-actor aggregates (issue #28) can slice by it. Unlike `name`/`description`, `category` alone is retaggable after creation via PATCH /v1alpha1/runs/{id} (frame decision q4).

description.description: Optional operator-given free-text description (task t3). Set at creation only, like `name` — immutable afterward.

input.description: The run input. Validated against the workflow's input contract.

name.description: Optional operator-given display name (task t3, migrations/0013). Additive: omitting it (every pre-t3 client) behaves exactly as before. Set at creation only — there is no way to change it afterward; see PatchRunRequest.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. An operator who declared a cadence and did not say otherwise meant it to run.

first_fire_at.description: The first instant this schedule is due, and the phase every later occurrence aligns to. Omitted means one interval from now: creating a schedule is not the same act as starting a run.

attempt_ref.description: Narrows the verdict to one attempt.

command.description: The argv the gate actually executed, when it executed one itself. Absent when the verdict came from a suite run elsewhere.

commit_sha.description: The commit the suite ran against, full 40-character lowercase hex. `HEAD`, a branch name, and an abbreviated sha are all refused: each means something different tomorrow, and a verdict that does not name what it tested is not evidence.

exit_code.description: The number the suite exited with. Required and never defaulted — an omitted exit code reading as 0 would make every malformed request a pass. Zero records verdict `confirm`; anything else records `reject`. The label is computed here, never supplied.

implicated_paths.description: Repo-relative paths the gate knows this failure involves, added to the ones the control plane already measured for the run's handover. A failure implicating `.github/` routes to a human: a repair attempt is a dispatch, and a dispatch may not modify CI configuration.

node_run_ref.description: Narrows the verdict to one node run.

ref.description: The handover ref that carried the commit, when one did. Validated against the same `refs/culture-nodes/` fence a control-plane fetch is, so a verdict cannot name a ref the collector was never allowed to fetch.

repair_actor_id.description: Overrides which lane a repair would be routed to. Omit it to use the actor that authored this run's claims — the party that has the checkout the failure is in.

requires_grants.description: The dispatch grants the SUITE needs beyond running its own binary (`network-egress`, `home-write`, ...), in the vocabulary the bridges' capability surface uses. Only a routing input, never part of the verdict record. The gate is the only party that knows its suite talks to a database, and a repair lane whose posture grants no egress cannot verify one — so declaring it here is what turns #119 into a routing decision rather than a wasted session.

suite.description: What ran, in the spelling a reader could re-run it with ("go test ./...", "uv run pytest -n auto", a CI job name). An unnamed suite cannot be re-run, so an empty one is refused.

validator_actor_id.description: The registered actor identifying the deterministic producer. Must not be an actor registered as `human` — a person reporting a suite result is making a claim about it, not producing it.

currency.description: Omitted when the summarized attempt(s) reported a cost with no currency at all.

decider_actor_id.description: The human actor this decision is attributed to. Recorded as the ledger decision record's origin and the confirming review's reviewer_actor_id.

expected_ledger_version.description: The run's ledger version the decider last read. A mismatch is refused with 409, nothing written.

outcome.description: The domain outcome selected. Must be one of the task's allowed_outcomes.

record_ids.description: Other ledger records the decider is confirming alongside this decision (e.g. records the task's context_refs pointed at). Ordinarily empty.

response.description: The decision payload — notes, the decision schema's filled-in fields, whatever the presenting surface collected. Also the CEL "output" activation for a guarded edge leaving this node.

emitter.description: Free text naming who emitted the fact (an actor ref, a node id, an external system). Attribution for operators, never an authority claim (PRD §10.4) — an inbound event is actor-reported information, not observed evidence. Defaults to `external`.

name.description: The signal name until.signal subscriptions match on.

payload.description: The emitter's free-form event body. Folded into the resumed wait node's output so downstream bindings can read it. Defaults to `{}`.

run_id.description: Optional scope. Set, the event resumes only that run's matching subscriptions; unset, it resumes every matching subscription in the namespace.

source_key.description: Stable emitter-owned identity whose watermark suppresses duplicate deliveries. Must be supplied with watermark.

subject.description: Optional correlation key (e.g. a Jira issue key) distinct from source_key/watermark's exact-redelivery cursor — two different real events on the same subject are both appended, but if the event matches a trigger and an ACTIVE run already exists for (workflow, subject), the event attaches to that run instead of creating a sibling (see triggered[].attached).

watermark.description: Opaque per-source position. An exact repeat for source_key returns the original event without delivering it again.

path.description: A JSON Pointer into the submitted document.

DialInCredential.description:
This actor key's `inbound_authentication` state (migrations 0031, 0032, 0037). Absent entirely when no record exists — the actor could not dial in even if its process were healthy.
An actor can look absent for four unrelated reasons: its process is down, its credential was revoked, it is locked out after repeated failures, or it was never issued a control-plane credential. Only the first is an outage, and they look identical in presence alone.
No verifier material is rendered here — not the digest, not the environment variable name. Neither is needed to answer "why is this bridge not dialling in".

issued.description: Whether THIS control plane minted the credential (migration 0037's `issued_at`). False means the record was provisioned by hand, which the shipped admission default refuses as `not_control_plane_issued` — such a bridge never dials in successfully however healthy its process is.

locked_out.description: Computed against this response's `observed_at`, the same way ActorAvailability.paused is computed server-side. A lapsed lockout renders `false` with `locked_until` still present — distinct from a credential never locked out at all, which carries no `locked_until`.

revoked_at.description: Revocation is positive durable evidence (migration 0032), so it renders as an instant rather than as an inference from absence.

DialInPresence.description: One registered actor identity's dial-in state. Keyed by `actor_key`, not by an actors-table row id: registration is append-only, so one identity has many revisions and exactly one connection.

actor_id.description: The current (highest) registration revision's row id, so a row here can be followed to GET /v1alpha1/actors/{id}.

last_seen_at.description: The last poll. Present for `connected` and `disconnected`, absent for `never_dialled`. On a dropped connection this is the whole answer: it says WHEN, which a boolean cannot.

presence.description: Three values on purpose. `never_dialled` (no presence row at all) is a configuration or deployment fact; `disconnected` is a bridge that HAS dialled in and stopped, which is an outage. A two-valued present/absent answer would report a bridge nobody ever configured and a bridge that died an hour ago identically.

seconds_since_last_seen.description: Absent — never `0` — when nothing was ever seen; a fabricated zero there would read as "seen just now".

DialInPresenceList.description: GET /v1alpha1/dial-in-presence' payload (task t6). The three counts are not client-side convenience: the address-retirement cutover's fallback-disable step must establish that every bridge is dialled in AT THAT MOMENT, and `connected == items.length` is that check in one read.

observed_at.description: The single instant every item was classified against, so two rows in one response never disagree about "now".

window_seconds.description: How recently a bridge must have polled to count as `connected`. Published because "connected" is a claim with a definition, and it is the same window dispatch resolution uses.

DispatchRate.description:
One dispatch-rate scope's declared rate and its standing in the CURRENT session window (task t10, migration 0022's `dispatch_rate_state`). On an actor payload it is that actor's own rate, resolved by `actor_key` the way `availability` is, and absent when no declared rate has ever admitted a dispatch to it.

`window_started_at`, `window_ends_at`, `dispatched` and `remaining` are computed against the moment of the read, not read raw from the row: session windows reset on a fixed clock, so a stored counter belonging to a window that has already ended reports zero consumption rather than showing last window's spending as though it still constrained anything. `last_dispatch_at` and `updated_at` stay raw row provenance, so that history is not lost either.

dispatched.description: Dispatches admitted in the current window.

limit_per_window.description: Dispatches one window may admit, as the last worker to consume a slot enforced it. Workers that disagree about the configured rate show up here rather than being averaged away.

next_dispatch_at.description: The pace, made durable: the earliest instant the next dispatch in this scope may go. Absent when nothing has dispatched yet.

remaining.description: How many more dispatches this scope may admit before the window ends: the remaining-window capacity capped by the remaining budget. It shrinks as the window runs out even when nothing has been consumed, because the control spreads sessions across the REMAINING window rather than at a rate that ignores when the window ends (spec claim c43).

scope.description: `global` (the whole installation's session rate) or `actor` (one actor key's own).

scope_key.description: The actor key for scope `actor`; absent for `global`.

window_anchor.description: The reset clock: an instant at which a window boundary falls. Every boundary is this instant plus or minus a whole number of windows, which is how horizontally-scaled workers agree on which window they are in without exchanging a message.

window_ends_at.description: When that window resets and the budget returns.

window_started_at.description: The start of the window this rate is in right now.

Error.description: The stable error shape, every non-2xx response, every operation. Mirrors internal/clifmt.CliError's JSON encoding exactly: `code` follows the same exit-code-style bucket (1 = domain/user error such as not-found or conflict, 2 = environment error such as a database outage), and the HTTP status line carries the specific condition.

duplicate.description: True when source_key and watermark already named a recorded event; resumed, picked_up, and triggered are then empty.

picked_up.description: Every event route this delivery reached (issue #43). An admitted entry created a token and a node run at the route's target; a refused entry created nothing and says why — its guard declined, or the pickup would have taken the run past one of its spec.limits bounds. A refused pickup is deliberately NOT a run failure: an external event must not kill a healthy run because it arrived at a busy moment.

refusal.description: "guard", "run_terminal", or the loop bound that had no headroom (max_parallel_tokens, max_visits_per_node, max_transitions).

resumed.description: Every waiting subscription this delivery fired. Empty is a normal answer — the event was recorded and nothing was waiting.

triggered.description: Matching workflow-level handlers, one entry per match. Empty means no newest published workflow version matched; the event is still recorded.

attached.description: True when run_id names a run that already existed for this event's subject — the trigger matched but no new run was created; the event was recorded on the existing run instead. False/absent means run_id is a brand-new run.

deferred.description: True when the workflow's configured limits.maxConcurrentSubjectRuns ceiling had no headroom for a new subject — no run was created and run_id is empty. deferred_trigger_id names the queued row a later matching event for this subject, or a run of this workflow reaching a terminal state, will drain into a run.

deferred_trigger_id.description: Set exactly when deferred is true.

ticket_status.description: The board status the caller observed on the ticket, e.g. "Done" or "In Progress" (task t17). "Done" (case-insensitive) cancels the ticket's runs; anything else, including an absent value, parks them. Supplied rather than looked up: the Jira bridge has no read verb.

cancelled_runs.description: Ids of the runs this freeze cancelled, in creation order.

freeze.description: What the freeze did to this ticket's runs. Present only on a frozen ticket.

parked_runs.description: Ids of the runs this freeze parked, in creation order.

GateMeasurement.description: The number an applicable gate produced and the threshold it was measured against. The threshold travels with the result because it is pinned in the published workflow — a reader must be able to see it was not chosen after the number was known.

GateNotApplicable.description: Why a declared gate measured nothing, and what it left uncovered.

reason.description: The vocabulary is closed so "which trees does no instrument reach yet" stays a query rather than a read. `instrument_unavailable` is the reason that makes the whole report `measurement_incomplete`: the instrument was expected to reach this change and did not get the chance.

uncovered_paths.description: The changed files this instrument did not cover. Required for every reason but `no_source_files`: a not-applicable gate that names nothing is indistinguishable from a gate nobody ran, and would read as a pass by omission.

GateRepairMetadata.description: What a repair of THIS gate would need, declared by the gate that knows. Routing input only; never part of the record.

GateReportEntry.description: One declared gate's finding. Exactly one of `exit_code` and `not_applicable` must be present.

changed_files_considered.description: The changed files this gate's applicability decision was made against, so a reader can check the decision rather than take it.

exit_code.description: The number the gate exited with. Present only for a gate that ran; zero records `passed`, anything else `failed`.

gate.description: The gate's name in the workflow's declared matrix ("go-test", "coverage", "web-build"). An unnamed gate cannot be counted.

instrument.description: The tool that produced (or failed to produce) the measurement.

instrument_version.description: The instrument's version, when one could be read. Often absent for a not-applicable gate precisely BECAUSE the instrument was unavailable.

suite.description: What ran, or would have, in the spelling a reader could re-run it with. Defaults to the gate name for a gate that ran.

GateReportResult.description:
The records the report produced, and the outcome computed over them.

`outcome` and `exit_code` are echoed because they are the two values the gate program and the control plane must agree about: the program exits with the code, the workflow routes on the outcome, and a caller that computed a different one should find out here rather than from a run that took the wrong edge.

exit_code.description: The exit code that outcome is reported with (0/1/2). It is the contract between the gate program and the code node's declared outcomes.

outcome.description: The gate node's domain outcome, computed from the per-gate statuses. A threshold miss is `changes_required` — a domain answer that follows an edge, never an engine failure.

routing_errors.description: Routings that were computed but could not be recorded, stated rather than omitted.

routings.description: The derived repair routings composed for the rejecting gates.

HumanTask.description: One human_tasks row (PRD §9.9): what an approval node's dispatch wrote instead of enqueuing work. `request` carries every field the PRD says the task must contain that is not already one of this object's own properties — decision_schema_ref, approver_ref, deadline, allowed_outcomes, context_refs, audit — exactly as the engine stored it, so a reader sees precisely what the human was shown.

node_run_id.description: The paused node run this task belongs to.

request.description: The PRD §9.9 task payload (decision_schema_ref, approver_ref, deadline, allowed_outcomes, context_refs, audit).

response.description: Set once the task is decided — outcome, decider_actor_id, response, decided_at.

ledger_records.description: The proposed decision record and the confirming review record the review transaction appended.

next_human_task_id.description: Set instead of a claimable work item when the routed edge itself reaches another approval node.

node_run_id.description: The node run the decision resolved.

run_output.description: Set only when the routed edge ended the run.

InboundCompletion.description: POST /v1alpha1/inbound/{id}/complete' body: the local handler's answer, relayed verbatim. The control plane parses `status` and `body` together as the invocation response the waiting dispatch receives, so an error from the local handler is reported by sending ITS status and ITS body here — not by omitting the completion.

body.description: The local handler's response body, as JSON. Required: an absent `body` is a 400. It is stored raw and parsed as the invocation response, so it must be the handler's actual payload rather than a summary of it.

status.description: The HTTP status the bridge's local handler returned. Must be 100-599; anything outside that is a 400.

InboundCredentialPartyRequest.description:
The body of BOTH credential operations, and the whole body: which party. No field may carry credential material — the control plane chooses the value.
Seven field names are declared honeypots (`credential`, `token`, `secret`, `verifier`, `verifier_sha256`, `verifier_env_name`, `digest_sha256`): sending any of them is a 400 that NAMES the offending field and tells the caller to remove it. They are checked in a fixed order, so a request carrying two of them is always refused by the same one. Unknown fields are refused too, just without the explanation — the honeypots exist to make the likely mistake legible.

party_key.description: For `actor`, an actor key: `namespace/name` (at least one slash; each segment `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`). For `host`, a host NAME. Address-shaped keys are refused on shape — a dotted quad, or anything containing `:` — so that an address-like typo cannot become durable identity even if one octet is out of range. The key travels here rather than in the path precisely because it contains a slash.

party_kind.description: Defaults to `actor` when omitted or empty. Note that the transport routes only ever authenticate `actor`, so a `host` credential is mintable but not dialable.

InboundEnvelope.description:
One unit of work claimed from `inbound_actor_mailbox` by POST /v1alpha1/inbound/poll — the mailbox envelope. Returned ONLY with 200; an idle poll answers 204 with an empty body and this schema is not involved.
The envelope is a wrapper, not the work: `request` is the payload, and the other three fields exist so the bridge can settle the envelope and label the work correctly.

actor_key.description: The party this envelope was addressed to — the same value the bridge sent in `X-Culture-Nodes-Actor-Key`.

attempt_id.description: The protocol attempt id, and the value the bridge MUST forward to its local invocation handler as the `Idempotency-Key` header. That is what makes a redelivery safe: an envelope whose 90-second claim lease expires becomes claimable again, so the same attempt can legitimately reach the bridge more than once, and the local handler's replay store is what turns the second arrival into the first arrival's recorded response instead of a second billable run. The bridge does not invent this key and must not substitute the envelope `id` for it — a fresh key per delivery would defeat the whole mechanism.

id.description: The mailbox row id, and the ONLY value that addresses POST /v1alpha1/inbound/{id}/complete. Do not send `attempt_id` there.

request.description: The invocation request, verbatim, to be POSTed to the bridge's own local invocation endpoint. Opaque here on purpose: the control plane stores what it marshalled and this operation is transport, not interpretation.

IssuedInboundCredential.description: POST /v1alpha1/inbound/credentials' 201 body. The `credential` field is the one and only time the plaintext leaves the process: it is held in a self-redacting secret type until this response is written, the reveal zeroes its buffer, and no operation on this API can return it again. Capture it at issuance or issue a new one.

credential.description: The plaintext, `cnd_` + base64url of 32 crypto/rand bytes. The prefix makes a leaked value recognisable to a secret scanner without disclosing anything — all the entropy is after it. Present exactly once, here.

digest_sha256.description: The SHA-256 verifier, hex. This is what the database holds, so returning it discloses nothing new; it lets an operator confirm which credential a stored record corresponds to.

issued_at.description: When the verifier row committed. The reveal happens only after this, so a credential in hand always has a verifier behind it.

revealed_once.description: Always `true`. It is a statement about the contract, not a mode to be varied: there is no configuration under which the value can be read a second time.

next_cursor.description: Opaque keyset pagination cursor. Present only when a further page exists; pass it back as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch it.

NodeRunListItem.description: One row of GET /v1alpha1/node-runs (task t11) — the same node_runs row NodeRun above documents, listed across every run in the namespace rather than nested under one, with `run_id` added (the parent run is not implied by a URL path here) and `actor_id` added (the most recent attempt's actor or runner reference; empty until the node run has been dispatched at least once) and `usage` added (task t2's §13.2 rollup over this node run's own attempts — always present, even a present-but-empty rollup for a node run with zero attempts).

actor_id.description: The actor or runner reference (attempts.actor_id) of this node run's most recently dispatched attempt.

PatchRunRequest.description: The only body PATCH /v1alpha1/runs/{id} accepts. `name` and `description` are immutable once a run is created (frame decision q4) — a request body carrying either key is refused with a structured 400, not silently ignored.

category.description: The run's new category tag. An empty string clears it. See CreateRunRequest.category for what this field means.

record_count.description: Undecided records across every listed run — the number a stage exit gate compares against zero.

data.description: The record's payload, verbatim — what the decider actually reads.

ledger_version.description: The run's current ledger version, read in this same request — what POST /v1alpha1/runs/{id}/reviews wants as `ledger_version`.

PlanImport.description: GET /v1alpha1/plan-imports/{id}' and the 201 body of POST /v1alpha1/plan-imports (task t22): one immutable import snapshot. Deliberately not a work-ledger record — see migrations/0024_plan_imports.sql.

slug.description: The source plan's own slug. NOT unique: re-importing the same slug creates a new, independent snapshot row.

source_digest.description: sha256 digest of the raw imported bytes.

source_slug.description: The source document/frame this plan was decomposed from (devague `frame_slug`).

source_status.description: The source system's own plan-level status verbatim.

PlanImportDeviation.description: One execution-time deviation of an imported plan snapshot.

deviation_ref.description: The source system's own deviation id, e.g. devague's `d1`.

origin_kind.description: The issue #45 "system knows" (llm -> agent) vs "user reports" (user -> human) split, preserved verbatim from the source.

source_status.description: The source system's own deviation status verbatim (devague: `proposed` | `approved` | `rejected` — note `approved`, not `confirmed`) — never translated into a ledger authority value.

task_ref.description: The plan task this deviation relates to.

PlanImportRequest.description: POST /v1alpha1/plan-imports' body (task t22). `plan_show` is the exact object `devague plan show --json` prints (or an equivalent document from another source system — this surface is domain-agnostic, task t24 exercises a non-code one). `deviations`, when present, is the exact object `.devague/deliveries/<slug>.json` holds on disk, and its `plan_slug` must equal `plan_show.slug`.

deviations.description: Execution-time deviations from the confirmed plan, each carrying its origin (`user` or `llm` — the issue #45 "system knows" vs "user reports" split).

plan_show.description: The faithful per-task plan view: per-task status and REAL dependency edges, never a wave approximation.

PlanImportSummary.description: One row of GET /v1alpha1/plan-imports?slug= (task t23): the same plan-level fields PlanImport carries, without `tasks`/`deviations` — those are read one snapshot at a time via GET /v1alpha1/plan-imports/{id}.

PlanImportTask.description: One task of an imported plan snapshot.

depends_on.description: REAL per-task dependency edges: other tasks' `task_ref` values in this same plan import, exactly as the source recorded them — never widened to "everything in the previous wave".

origin_kind.description: The ledger producer kind the source's own origin maps to (devague `user` -> `human`, `llm` -> `agent`).

source_status.description: The source system's own per-task decision status verbatim (devague: `proposed` | `confirmed` | `rejected`) — never translated into a ledger authority value.

task_ref.description: The source system's own task id, e.g. devague's `t3`.

wave.description: Computed LOCALLY at import time via topological layering over depends_on — the source system does not emit this field itself. Absent for a rejected task, which occupies no wave.

Preflight.description: One clarify-then-commit briefing (task t14, issue #67; migration 0026's `dispatch_preflights`). `expired` is computed against the server clock at read time, because the window — not the row's existence — is the predicate everywhere in this feature.

acknowledgement_record_id.description: The proposed `dispatch_acknowledgement` record carrying the claim.

actor_id.description: The actors-table row id, present only when the registry could resolve one. Absent means unattributed, never a fabricated id.

actor_key.description: The actor identity this dispatch is addressed to.

consumed.description: True once a dispatch has ridden this briefing. Single-use: the next dispatch of that node needs its own.

document.description: The briefing itself, as the derived ledger record carries it. Present on the detail and acknowledge responses; omitted from list items.

record_digest.description: That record's content digest. An acknowledgement names it, so "the actor acknowledged this briefing" cannot later be true of a briefing whose content the reader never saw.

record_id.description: The `dispatch_preflight` ledger record stating the briefing.

summary.description: Populated only by the delivery_summary projection.

RegisterActorRequest.description: POST /v1alpha1/actors' body (task t13). The row's `id` and `revision` are never the caller's to choose: the id is minted server-side and the revision is always the next one for `actor_key`. `capabilities` and `metadata` follow the Actor schema's credential rule — `metadata.auth_token_env`, when set, names the environment variable a worker reads a token from, never the token value itself.

capabilities.description: Declared capabilities, stored as the row's JSON value ('{}' when omitted).

kind.description: The actor kind (e.g. agent, human, runner).

metadata.description: Open metadata, stored as the row's JSON value ('{}' when omitted).

namespace.description: Optional. This server is bound to one namespace at construction; when present, this may only name that namespace's id — anything else is refused with 400 rather than silently rerouted.

ResumeActorRequest.description: POST /v1alpha1/actors/{id}/resume' body (task t9). Entirely optional: no body, an empty body, and `{}` all mean "an operator did this and did not say who", recorded as `cleared_by: operator` rather than as an empty attribution.

cleared_by.description: Who is clearing the pause, recorded on the availability row. Defaults to `operator`.

revoked_at.description: When authority ENDED. Re-revoking returns the original instant rather than moving it, because that is the fact being recorded.

actor.description: The actor reference this node dispatched to.

rule.description: The declared affinity rule that chose it, if it was named.

actor_affinity.description:
The routing this run's workflow declared and resolved at creation (task t33, issue #107, migrations/0033), keyed by node id — e.g. `{"fix": {"actor": "actor://company/developer", "rule": "security-findings"}}`. Absent when the run resolved none, which is the case both for a workflow that declares no `spec.affinity` and for a run created by an operator rather than by an event trigger (affinity conditions are evaluated against the triggering event, so a run with no event has nothing to evaluate them against).

`rule` is the declared affinity rule's name, and it is carried rather than dropped because it is what the per-actor comparative record slices by: "actor X ran this node" is already recoverable from the attempt, but "actor X was chosen because the workflow classified this as security-findings work" is only recoverable from here.

category.description: The run's flat category tag (task t3), if any. Retaggable via PATCH /v1alpha1/runs/{id} (frame decision q4).

description.description: Operator-given free-text description (task t3). Immutable after creation.

display_hint.description: A truncated, best-effort guess at what this run is about, derived AT READ TIME from a request/instruction/task-ish top-level string field of the run's own input — never persisted, and present only when `name` is absent. A client MUST treat this as distinct from `name`: it is a guess, not something an operator actually said, and must never be presented to a user as if it were the given name.

name.description: Operator-given display name (task t3). Absent when the run was created without one — see `display_hint` for a derived fallback. Immutable after creation.

output.description: The run's result. Present only once the run has completed.

reason.description:
Why the run is in this state, when the state was a CONTROL-PLANE decision rather than something an actor reported (task t17, migrations/0052). Today's one writer is the ticket freeze: a run whose subject is a frozen ticket reads `"reason": "ticket_frozen"` beside a `cancelled` or `waiting` state.

Absent for every run that reached its state the ordinary way, where the account of what happened is the last attempt's own `result.error.detail` (task t6). The two are deliberately separate fields: an attempt's result is the ACTOR's evidence and is immutable, so a control-plane decision is never written over it.

subject.description: The triggering event's correlation key (task t15, migrations/0038, spec c31/h16) — e.g. a Jira issue key. Absent for an operator-created run, or a triggered run whose event carried none. When present, POST /v1alpha1/events attaches a LATER matching event on the same subject to this run instead of creating a sibling (see EventDeliveryResult.triggered[].attached) — this is what makes "exactly one active run per subject" (spec c31) a fact GET /v1alpha1/runs/{id} can show.

usage.description: The run-wide §13.2 usage/cost rollup (task t2), summed over every attempt of every node run in this run. Always present on GET /v1alpha1/runs/{id} (getRun), POST /v1alpha1/runs (createRun), PATCH /v1alpha1/runs/{id} (patchRun), and POST /v1alpha1/runs/{id}/cancel (cancelRun) — even a freshly created run with zero attempts carries a present-but-empty rollup, never an absent field. NOT computed (and therefore absent) on GET /v1alpha1/runs (listRuns), which would otherwise need one extra query per listed row.

workflow_key.description: The stable key of the workflow version pinned by this run. Present in run listings.

next_cursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor for the next page; absent on the last page.

RunView.description: The Run-view payload (PRD §8.6 Run, §8.7 first visual slice): the run itself, every token, and every node run with its attempts nested — one round trip for the whole graph position and history.

catch_up.description:
What to do about an occurrence that came due while nothing was running — the question a cron line never answers.

`fire-once` (the default) fires late, exactly once, then realigns to the next declared boundary; missed occurrences are counted, never backfilled, because six queued runs would each carry the same freshly-read findings. `skip` declines a MISSED occurrence and waits for the next boundary, which is right for anything whose value is tied to when it happens — a nightly report has no business running at noon. A skip increments `skip_count` and emits `dev.culture.nodes.schedule.skipped`, so "chose not to run" and "never came due" stay distinguishable.

The two differ ONLY for a missed occurrence. One that is merely LATE — overdue by less than one whole interval, which a tick interval and a busy loop produce normally — fires under both.

emitter.description: Free text naming who emitted the fact. Attribution for operators, never an authority claim (PRD §10.4).

event_name.description: The signal event this schedule appends on each occurrence.

last_event_id.description: The `signal_events` fact the last fire appended — the audit trail in one field, since the runs it triggered are reachable from it.

last_failure_detail.description: The repeated reason, verbatim: the last minted run's last attempt's `result.error.detail` (falling back to that attempt's technical status, then the run's, when the attempt reported no error envelope). Absent when the schedule is not currently failing, so its presence is the answer to "is this schedule holding back, and why".

name.description: Unique per namespace. It is the handle an operator disables by, which is why two schedules cannot share one.

next_fire_at.description: The next instant this schedule is due, and the whole durable state of the loop: it is advanced only inside the transaction that also appends the event, which is what makes a restart unable to double-start or lose an occurrence.

payload.description: The event body, verbatim. Plain declared data — a schedule reads no external system and holds no credential.

skip_count.description: Occurrences declined under a `skip` catch-up policy.

suppressed_count.description:
Due occurrences this schedule held back because its last two minted runs failed with the SAME reason (task t9, issue #253).

Suppression is a rate, not a stop: a suppressed schedule still mints a probe run at most every `NODES_SCHEDULE_PROBE_INTERVAL` (default 30m), so a repaired environment is discovered without an operator resuming anything, and one completed run puts the schedule straight back on its declared cadence. `enabled` therefore keeps its own meaning — an operator said stop — while this counter records the environment saying stop.

Counted rather than inferred, and separate from `skip_count`, because "the operator declared a catch-up policy" and "the work keeps failing identically" are different answers to "why has nothing run".

run_id.description: Present only when the event was run-scoped.

StoreBinding.description: One binding record: which graph-pinned requirement was bound to which local registration (row id current at bind time + key), by whom, when. Append-only; the current binding per ref is the newest record.

StoreBindingCreateRequest.description: Bind one declared capability requirement (`ref`, verbatim from the entry's evidence manifest) to the local registration `actor_key` names. `bound_by` identifies who declared the mapping — a binding is a record.

StoreCapabilityRequirement.description: One actor/runner capability the graph pins. `ref` is the graph's pinned identifier (actor://…, runner://…) carried verbatim; `capabilities` is what a substitute registration on an importing plane must advertise. Requirements live here — in the evidence manifest — never as graph rewrites, so an import can bind them to local registrations without touching the graph document or its digest.

StoreDeviationRecordRef.description: A pointer to one deviation record recorded against the flow — a tree path (docs/deviations/…) or URL, carried verbatim.

StoreEntry.description: One catalog entry: a graph plus its evidence. `entry_digest` is the canonical digest of the entry's portable content (name + graph + evidence) — per-plane row identity (id, origin, source_registry, created_at) is excluded, which is what makes re-pulls idempotent and lets a pulling plane verify integrity.

source_registry.description: Where a pulled entry came from; absent on local entries.

StoreEntryCreateRequest.description: Catalog a locally proven flow. `name` defaults to the workflow key of the version `graph_digest` resolves to.

StoreEntryGraph.description: The graph half of an entry. `source` is present on the single-entry document (which must be self-contained enough to republish elsewhere) and omitted from listings.

StoreEntryPullRequest.description: Ingest an entry fetched from another registry. `entry` is the full document that registry's GET /v1alpha1/store/entries/{id} served, verbatim; `source_registry` names where it was fetched from and is recorded on the row.

StoreEvidenceManifest.description: The full-fidelity evidence half of a store entry: the prod run ids that proved the flow, the deviation records recorded against it, and the capability requirements its graph pins.

SuiteVerdictResult.description:
What the gate produced: the suite's verdict, and — for a REJECTING gate — where that failure was routed (task t32, issue #102).

Two records rather than one because a rejecting gate produces two facts, and splitting them across two round trips would put the operator back in the loop the routing exists to take them out of.

`routing` is absent for a passing gate: there is nothing to route, and a ledger row per green gate saying so is noise. `routing_error` is present, with `routing` still absent, when a routing was computed but could not be recorded — the verdict is the primary record and is never failed to protect its derivation, but the failure is stated rather than left as a silence.

routing_error.description: Why the gate failure was not recorded as routed. Overwhelmingly this is a repair-router producer identity nobody registered — `ledger_records.origin_actor_id` has a foreign key to `actors(id)`.

human_tasks.description: Every human task on the ticket's runs, in any status.

pending_tasks.description: The decidable subset of human_tasks. Both are served because they answer different questions — what was asked, and what is still being asked.

ticket_url.description: Where this ticket lives on the board, composed from the Jira work-item fact the ticket's runs carry (`details_url`, else `jira_site` plus the key), falling back to a posted frame's own `ticket_url`/`jira_url` (task t18, spec c10). Always an absolute http(s) URL; absent when nothing this projection can see says where the ticket lives.

banner.description: The sentence the ticket page renders under its frozen heading, naming both counts and the reason. Composed server-side so the count a human reads is the count the API test asserts.

cancelled_runs.description: How many of the ticket's runs are cancelled carrying that reason. Derived at read time from the runs in this same projection, never a stored tally that could disagree with them.

parked_runs.description: How many of the ticket's runs are parked (`waiting`) carrying that reason.

reason.description: The run-level reason stamped on every run this freeze ended (`ticket_frozen`).

ticket_status.description: The board status the freeze was decided against, as the caller reported it. Absent means the caller did not say — which is why the runs were parked rather than cancelled.

TicketPendingTask.description: One pending human task on a ticket, shaped for the surface that decides it (task t18). Every field is read back out of the task's own recorded request — what the human was actually shown (PRD §9.9) — never re-derived from the workflow.

allowed_outcomes.description: Exactly the outcomes POST /human-tasks/{id}/decision will accept. Always present; an EMPTY array means this task declares none (an alert rather than a choice, e.g. `schedule_failing`) and must be distinguishable from an omitted field.

deadline.description: When this task becomes overdue. Absent when the node declared none.

ledger_version.description: The run's ledger version READ IN THIS REQUEST, which is what a decision must submit as `expected_ledger_version`. Served with the task so the version a decider attests to is the one the page they read was rendered from.

origin_event_id.description: The signal event that created this token, set only on an event pickup (issue #43). A pickup token has no parent token — nothing in the run handed it control, and the emitter may be another run entirely — so it names the fact it came from instead. A consumer drawing the ancestry tree must tolerate several roots per run and label the ones carrying this field.

Usage.description: The §13.2 usage/cost rollup task t2 aggregates from attempts (see migrations/0012_attempt_usage.sql) attempt→node-run→run, over EVERY attempt in scope regardless of technical outcome — a failed or cancelled attempt that still burned tokens before ending still counts ("retry burn"). Cost is summed only over attempts that reported one, and never across differing currencies: `cost` + `currency` are set together only when every cost-reporting attempt in scope agreed on one currency; `cost_by_currency` is set instead, as a list, whenever more than one currency was seen.

attempts_not_reported.description: How many attempts in scope completed with no usage block reported. attempts_reported == 0 with attempts_not_reported > 0 is "no attempt reported usage" — distinct from a reported sum that happens to equal zero (attempts_reported > 0, input_tokens == 0).

attempts_reported.description: How many attempts in scope reported a usage block at all.

cache_ratio.description: cached_input_tokens / input_tokens, present only when input_tokens > 0. Never computed as a fabricated 0 when no attempt in scope reported any input tokens (0/0 is undefined, not zero) — absent in that case.

cached_input_tokens.description: docs/adr/0009-usage-telemetry-extension.md: summed over attempts that reported this field specifically. An attempt that reported input/output tokens but no cache telemetry at all (its contract exposes none) contributes nothing here — never a fabricated zero standing in for "unmeasurable". This is not gated by its own reported/not-reported count; attempts_reported/attempts_not_reported below remains the one coverage signal for the whole usage block.

cost.description: Set only when every cost-reporting attempt in scope agreed on one currency (see `currency`); unset when no attempt reported a cost, or when currencies differ (see `cost_by_currency`).

cost_by_currency.description: Present instead of `cost`/`currency` when cost-reporting attempts in scope used more than one currency — one entry per currency actually seen, never summed together.

currency.description: Present alongside `cost` when the reporting attempts agreed on one currency. May be absent even when `cost` is set, meaning the reporting attempt(s) priced their work without naming a currency.

input_tokens.description: Summed over attempts that reported usage at all (attempts_reported below). An attempt that reported none contributes nothing here — never folded in as zero.

Version.description: The control plane's own build identity (task t32, issue #104).

revision.description: The commit this binary was built from. ABSENT when nothing established one — never an empty string, and never an abbreviation or a branch name.

revision_is_dirty.description: True when the Go toolchain stamped this build from a checkout with uncommitted changes, so the revision names the last commit and not the code that is running. Absent for a `build_flag` revision, which cannot know it — its absence is not a claim that the tree was clean.

revision_source.description: How the revision was learned. `build_flag` is what the deploy said it was building (`-ldflags -X main.revision`), which is the only thing that can answer inside a container built from a `git archive` with no .git in it. `go_vcs_stamp` is what the build machine observed, available only for a build that ran inside a checkout — and it is the only one that can also report `revision_is_dirty`.

staleness.description: One sentence on what this answer does and does not establish, including the case where the revision cannot be established at all.

source.description: The workflow document, in the given format.

digest.description: The content digest of the normalized IR. Empty when the document has error diagnostics.

normalized_ir.description: The normalized IR, as a JSON value.

actorRegistrationBearerAuth.description: The shared secret configured as NODES_ACTOR_REGISTRATION_TOKEN_SECRET. Used only by POST /v1alpha1/actors (task t13) — deliberately its own secret, not the decision secret, so an operator can grant registration standing without also granting the power to decide human tasks.

adhocRunBearerAuth.description: The shared secret configured as NODES_ADHOC_RUN_TOKEN_SECRET. Used only by POST /v1alpha1/adhoc-runs (task t19, gated by the t15 auth-hardening pass, spec c27) — its own secret, so the power to start ad-hoc (often billable) work is granted independently of decision, registration, and event standing.

attemptCallbackBearerAuth.description: The short-lived callback token minted for exactly one attempt. The route verifies it against the attempt id in the path before loading durable invocation authority or reading the request body.

decisionBearerAuth.description: The shared secret configured as NODES_HUMAN_DECISION_TOKEN_SECRET. Used by the three operations that record a human decision — POST /v1alpha1/human-tasks/{id}/decision and the two review operations (POST /v1alpha1/runs/{id}/reviews, POST /v1alpha1/reviews/{id}/commit) — because all three write human-authority records into the ledger on whoever presents the token. Every other operation in this API is authless by phase-1 design (spec decision c45).

eventBearerAuth.description: The shared secret configured as NODES_EVENT_TOKEN_SECRET. Used only by POST /v1alpha1/events (task t10) — its own secret again, so an external system granted the standing to emit signal events (which can resume any signal-parked run) holds neither decision nor registration power.

inboundActorKeyAuth.description: Names the party whose credential is being presented — an actor key (`namespace/name`), which is also the mailbox partition the poll claims from and the completion is scoped to. Required together with inboundDialBearerAuth: an absent or empty header is a 401 before the credential is examined at all. The transport routes hardcode the party KIND to `actor`, so a `host`-kind credential cannot dial in even though issuance will mint one.
inboundActorKeyAuth.name: X-Culture-Nodes-Actor-Key

inboundDialBearerAuth.description: The credential the control plane ISSUED for one dialling party — the `cnd_`-prefixed value returned exactly once by POST /v1alpha1/inbound/credentials. Presented by a bridge on every poll and every completion, alongside inboundActorKeyAuth; neither header is sufficient alone. Verified against a SHA-256 verifier read from PostgreSQL per call, never cached, which is what makes revocation effective on the next dial.

inboundIssuanceBearerAuth.description: The shared secret configured as NODES_INBOUND_ISSUANCE_TOKEN_SECRET. Used only by POST /v1alpha1/inbound/credentials and POST /v1alpha1/inbound/credentials/revoke (issue #111's dial-in half) — its own secret again, so the standing to mint or end a bridge's IDENTITY is granted independently of decision, registration, event and ad-hoc power. Absent configuration leaves both routes refusing with 401 rather than mounted-but-authless.

storeWriteBearerAuth.description: The shared secret configured as NODES_STORE_TOKEN_SECRET. Used only by the flow store's two write routes — POST /v1alpha1/store/entries and POST /v1alpha1/store/entries/pull (task t7, issue #192) — its own secret, so the standing to write the catalog is granted independently of decision, registration, event, and ad-hoc power. Store reads take no secret at all: the registry is an internal, mesh-private surface whose read side serves everyone on the mesh.

info.description:
The Culture Nodes control-plane API (docs/initial-design/culture-nodes-prd-spec.md §12.1, §15.1): workflow publication, run orchestration, the append-only work ledger, and review transactions. group: nodes.culture.dev/v1alpha1.
Phase 1 runs authless by design (spec decision c45): this API carries no authentication or authorization of its own and is meant to run behind a private network. Every operation is reachable by anyone who can reach the listener. Do not expose this API on a public network without a fronting proxy that adds authentication.
Every error response uses the Error schema below — the same {code, message, remediation} shape internal/clifmt.CliError renders for the CLI — with the HTTP status line carrying the specific condition. The two reverse-transport routes are the documented exception: POST /v1alpha1/inbound/poll and POST /v1alpha1/inbound/{id}/complete are not mounted through the wrapper that renders Error, so their 400/401 refusals are `text/plain` while their 500s still carry Error. Each of those responses says so where it is declared.
info.title: nodes.culture.dev/v1alpha1

get.description: Read-only (task t15): every `actors` table row, every revision — an actor_key's identity is append-only, so a capability or endpoint change is a new row, never an update to an existing one. Registering an actor is the authenticated POST on this same path (task t13).

200.description: Every registered actor row, ordered by actor_key then revision.

get.summary: List every registered actor row in this namespace.

post.description:
Task t13: the authenticated registration lane that replaces the raw-SQL-only deploy/prod/register-actor.sh path (issue #8). Registration is append-only, following that script's INSERT semantics: a first registration of an actor_key lands revision 1, and re-registering an existing actor_key inserts the next revision row — never an update to any existing row (actor identity, like ledger records, only ever appends).
Like the human-task decision endpoint — and unlike the rest of this authless-by-phase-1-design API (spec decision c45) — this operation requires a bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) matching the server's configured registration secret (`NODES_ACTOR_REGISTRATION_TOKEN_SECRET`, deliberately its own secret, not the decision secret): a registration row is what grants an endpoint the standing to be dispatched real work. An unauthenticated or wrongly authenticated request is refused with 401 before the body is even read.

201.description: The newly appended actor revision row.

400.description: The request is malformed, a required field is missing, or `namespace` names a namespace other than this server's own.

401.description: No bearer token was presented, it does not match the configured registration secret, or no secret is configured at all.

post.summary: Register an actor — append the next revision row for actor_key.

200.description: The actor row.

404.description: No actor with this id.

get.summary: Fetch one actor row by id.

post.description:
Task t9: the reversibility half of the capacity circuit breaker. When a dispatch to an actor fails with the `capacity_exhausted` §13.5 class, the worker marks that actor unavailable until a deadline and defers — never fails — work addressed to it. This operation ends that pause early, so an operator who knows better (the quota reset, the bridge was misreporting, the limit did not apply to this project) can overrule the automatic classification without touching the database.
The pause is keyed by `actor_key`, not by this row's id, so resuming any revision of an identity resumes the identity — provider capacity belongs to the identity, not to one append-only registration revision.
Clearing an actor that is not currently paused is 200 with the actor's current state, not an error: the caller's intent ("this actor should be dispatchable") is already satisfied, and two operators racing to clear one pause should both succeed.
Work items already deferred become claimable again within the worker's deferral horizon (at most a few minutes), not instantaneously: a deferral pushes `work_items.available_at` forward, and the horizon is bounded precisely so an early clear cannot go unnoticed for the whole pause.
Like actor registration on this same noun — and unlike the rest of this authless-by-phase-1-design API (spec decision c45) — it requires the actor-registration bearer token, deliberately the SAME secret (`NODES_ACTOR_REGISTRATION_TOKEN_SECRET`): registration is what grants an endpoint the standing to be dispatched real work, and clearing a pause restores exactly that standing.

200.description: The actor row, with its availability block reflecting the cleared pause.

401.description: No bearer token was presented, it does not match the configured registration secret, or no secret is configured at all.

404.description: No actor with this id.

post.summary: Clear a capacity pause early, making the actor dispatchable again.

get.description:
Task t6 (issues #136, #121): the read-only answer to the question a stored participant address used to answer. Every bridge dials OUT and the control plane records no address, so "is this bridge reachable?" becomes "is this bridge dialled in right now?" — and until this operation existed nothing answered it outside dispatch resolution, so an un-dialled bridge was discovered by a failing dispatch.
Nothing is dispatched and nothing is probed. Presence is a fact PostgreSQL already holds: a bridge polling `POST /v1alpha1/inbound/poll` refreshes its own `last_seen_at`, and this operation reads it. The control plane holds no address for a participant, so there is nothing to probe — reintroducing a probe would reintroduce the address.
`connected` means a poll within `window_seconds`, which is the SAME window dispatch resolution applies when it decides whether an actor is reachable through the durable mailbox. One definition, published in the response, so a reader can see what the claim means and the view can never say connected while dispatch says otherwise.
The spine is the actors table, not the presence table: an actor that has never dialled in has no presence row at all and would otherwise be silently missing from exactly the view an operator consults when a bridge is missing. `connected == items.length` is the check the cutover's fallback-disable step makes.

Task t10 (issue #48 item 2): the pacing control's read surface. A worker holds itself to a declared session rate — globally and per actor — against durable state every worker shares (migration 0022's `dispatch_rate_state`), because workers scale horizontally and an in-process limiter would enforce one rate per process rather than one rate.

This endpoint answers "why is this run sitting still" from the operator's side: the rate being enforced, how much of the CURRENT session window it has consumed, how much the rest of that window can still absorb, and when the next dispatch may go. Per deferral, the run's own event stream answers it too (`dev.culture.nodes.dispatch.paced`).

A scope with no recorded state is absent rather than rendered as a zeroed row: this surface reports what the workers have actually enforced, not what an environment somewhere claims to have configured. Read-only by design — a rate is the operator's own declaration, and it is changed by changing the workers' configuration (`NODES_DISPATCH_RATE_*`), not by an API that would then disagree with it.

200.description: Every rate scope with recorded state in this namespace.

The cross-run companion to GET /v1alpha1/runs/{id}/events (task t17): one SSE connection carrying committed events for every run in the namespace, instead of one connection per run — the data source for a live-mesh/board view that must not open one stream per displayed run.
Scope: by default, only events belonging to an ACTIVE (non-terminal) run, plus run-lifecycle events (run.created, run.completed, run.failed, run.cancelled, run.bounded) for any run — so a consumer sees runs appear and finish without being handed a completed run's full internal history it never asked to watch. Pass `runs` to override this default entirely and receive only events for the listed run ids, active or not.
Containment (risk r1): this handler polls at twice the per-run stream's interval, and each poll reads a bounded window of raw rows (ordered by the events table's own id) before applying the active-run/lifecycle filter — so one poll's cost never grows with how much of the namespace's history is currently terminal. See internal/api/events.go's handleStreamEvents for the full design note, including the documented catch-up behavior under a filtered backlog.
Resume by the events table's own id (a ULID, NOT the per-run `sequence` a single run's stream resumes on — there is no one sequence spanning multiple runs): send `Last-Event-ID` (a previously received `id:` field) to resume after a disconnect, or the `from` query parameter for a client that cannot set headers before its first connection. Each frame is `id: <ulid>
event: <type>
data: <envelope JSON>

`. Ordering promise: events are delivered in the order this control-plane process committed them (ULID generation order within one process, internal/store/ulid.go) — not a claim of a causally-ordered, cross-process global sequence.

Resumed runs complete through their normal edges — delivery makes the parked work item claimable again and a worker commits the completion through the ordinary engine transaction; delivery itself never completes anything.
An event with no waiting subscription is still appended — a fact, not an error; `resumed` is simply empty. A subscription created AFTER the event does not retroactively fire (documented limitation, issue #43): subscription-then-event resumes, event-then-subscription stays parked.
Requires a bearer token matching the server's configured event secret (`NODES_EVENT_TOKEN_SECRET`) — its own secret, separate from the decision and registration secrets, since emitting a named event can resume any signal-parked run in the namespace.

Validates outcome against the task's own allowed_outcomes (PRD §9.9), records the decision as a human-authority review through the same atomic, ledger-version-guarded review transaction PRD §10.8's review commit uses, transitions the waiting_human node run, and routes the edge the outcome selects — all in one transaction, or none of it. A task decides exactly once: a second decision on an already-decided task is refused with 409 rather than resuming the run again.
Unlike every other operation in this API — authless by phase-1 design, spec decision c45 — this one requires a bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) matching the server's configured decision secret (`NODES_HUMAN_DECISION_TOKEN_SECRET`): a decision here writes human authority into the run's ledger on whoever's behalf presents the token. An unauthenticated or wrongly authenticated request is refused with 401 before the body is even read.
